sections.overview: The lanner falcon is a medium-large falcon occurring across much of Africa, parts of southern Europe and southwest Asia.
sections.identification: Spain’s environment ministry describes a medium-sized falcon reaching up to 46 cm. Its plumage is paler than a peregrine’s, with a rufous crown and longer tail.
sections.habitat: It frequents steppe and desert as well as dry savanna; it usually nests on cliffs but may also use trees.
sections.diet: It hunts mainly birds, including pigeons and corvids, but also takes small mammals, reptiles and large insects.
sections.behavior: Pairs may hunt cooperatively, with one bird flushing prey while its partner waits to strike; populations are resident or partly migratory.
sections.reproduction: It usually reuses an old corvid or raptor nest on a cliff ledge or tree; clutches contain two to five eggs.
sections.ecology: Molecular research places it among the closely related hierofalcons and distinguishes its relationship to the peregrine from older classifications. The bestiary also profiles the Eurasian hobby, Falco subbuteo, another member of genus Falco.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN assessment is Least Concern, although the 2021 assessment reports a decreasing population trend.
